_comment: Declarative model selection policy for the intent layer (project 08). Data, not code — editing this file is not a deploy. Models are referenced by stable alias, never a pinned version ID. See docs/projects/08-intent-layer/spec.md (the 'Model selection policy' section) and src/intent/model-policy.ts.
_roleDefaults_comment: Per-role default model alias. `evaluator` (project 08, A6.2) resolves to an openai model so the autonomous Evaluator adjudicates cross-provider by default; the resolver also takes `distinctFromProvider` at call time, so an openai generator pushes the evaluator back to the anthropic globalFallback. The eight product-team roles (project 14, Phase 8): PM and tech lead → fable (anthropic, Fable 5), reviewer + designer + security → opus (anthropic, Opus 4.8), artifact roles → qa: gpt-5.6-terra, coder: gpt-5.6-sol (openai, via the Codex CLI); the resolver enforces reviewer-vs-coder provider distinctness at resolution time (fail-closed). `planning-critique` is the `/plan` cross-model critique pass — it must be a non-anthropic, coding-capable model because it runs through `runCodex` against a Claude-authored plan. `writer` drives the writing pipeline's plan/draft/critique/revise one-shots (SOUL + voice prose) — must stay claude-format (the calls go through the Claude CLI; writing-run-deps falls back to ONESHOT_MODEL otherwise). `adjudicator` breaks a reviewer-vs-tech-lead tie on a diff; its base model is a DECLARED choice, not a runtime distinctness computation — reviewer (opus) and tech lead (fable) are both anthropic, so the adjudicator sits on the openai side by design. It uses gpt-5.6-terra with fresh context. There is ONE adjudicator model. A task adjudicates at most once, whether it was triggered by an objection that survived a coder retry or by the round cap; both are last-call moments on a split that would otherwise end the task, so they do not warrant separate model bindings.
